title: Steve Jobs at Stanford 2005: connect the dots, love your work, remember death
summary: Jobs tells three stories: dropping in on a calligraphy class that later shaped the Mac's typography, being fired from Apple and finding it freeing, and facing cancer. The lessons: trust your curiosity and intuition, do only work you love, use mortality to cut through fear, and stay hungry and foolish.

principles.text: You can only connect the dots looking backward, so trust that curiosity and intuition will pay off later.
principles.quote: you can’t connect the dots looking forward; you can only connect them looking backwards. So you have to trust that the dots will somehow connect in your future.

principles.text: Follow curiosity even without practical payoff; it can become the foundation of great design.
principles.quote: None of this had even a hope of any practical application in my life. But ten years later, when we were designing the first Macintosh computer, it all came back to me.

principles.text: Great work requires loving what you do; keep looking and never settle.
principles.quote: the only way to be truly satisfied is to do what you believe is great work. And the only way to do great work is to love what you do. If you haven’t found it yet, keep looking. Don’t settle.

principles.text: Setbacks can free you: failure replaces the weight of success with the lightness of being a beginner.
principles.quote: The heaviness of being successful was replaced by the lightness of being a beginner again, less sure about everything. It freed me to enter one of the most creative periods of my life.

principles.text: Ask each morning if today were your last, would you do what you're about to do; change course if the answer is no too often.
principles.quote: If today were the last day of my life, would I want to do what I am about to do today?” And whenever the answer has been “No” for too many days in a row, I know I need to change something.

principles.text: Don't live someone else's life or let others' opinions drown out your inner voice.
principles.quote: Your time is limited, so don’t waste it living someone else’s life. Don’t be trapped by dogma—which is living with the results of other people’s thinking.
